chunks: What the Shaykh informed me of, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Abān, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from al-Qāsim, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from al-ʿAbd al-Ṣāliḥ عليه السلام, who said:

A slave-mother belonging to his father asked him and said: “May I be made your ransom, I want to ask you about something, but I am ashamed of it.” So he said: “Ask me, and do not be ashamed.” She said: “Menstrual blood got on my garment, and I washed it, but its trace did not go away.” He said: “Dye it with mishq until it blends in and its trace disappears.”

key_terms.أُمُّ وَلَدٍ: a slave-mother who bore a child

ai.seo_question: What should be done if the trace of menstrual blood remains on a garment after washing?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a ruling concerning a garment affected by menstrual blood when its visible trace remains after washing. The Imam عليه السلام instructs that it may be dyed with mishq so that the remaining trace blends in and disappears from sight.
